The range

Tapware in Sydney: mixers, spouts and showers

Tapware is the last thing chosen in most bathrooms and the first thing people notice. Choose the finish first, then the series, so every piece in the room matches.

Which tapware finish suits your bathroom?

FinishLookWearCleaning
ChromeBright and reflective. Suits any styleThe longest established finish, and easy to match laterShows water spots but wipes clean quickly
Brushed nickelSoft, warm silverA brushed surface hides fine scratchesHides fingerprints and water marks well
Matte blackStrong contrast against white basins and light tilesTake care with abrasive cloths, which can polish the surfaceShows soap and hard water marks, so wipe it dry
Gun metalDark grey, softer than blackA brushed dark surface hides marksHides fingerprints better than black
Modern brass and rosaWarm gold and rose tonesColoured finishes need gentle cleaningUse a soft cloth and mild soap only

General guidance on finishes. Follow the care instructions of the maker for the product you choose.

Mixers

Basin, wall and kitchen mixers

For the vanity, see basin mixers and taps, including wall mounted and high rise designs. For the shower or bath you need a wall mixer, and where one mixer feeds two outlets, look at combination mixers with a built-in diverter.

The 60 vessel mixers are listed on this page. They are taller mixers made for above counter basins. In the kitchen, choose a mixer for your sink from the same series as the bathroom tapware.

Pricing

Tapware prices

The tapware in this section shows Enquire Now. Add the products you want to your enquiry, with the finish, and the team confirms the price before you commit to anything.

No payment is taken online.

Finishes

Finishes: chrome, matt black, brushed nickel and gun metal

Most Millennium series are offered in six finishes: chrome, brushed nickel, matte black, gun metal, modern brass and rosa. That lets you carry one finish from the basin to the shower, the bath and the kitchen.

Finishes vary a little between makers, so a brushed nickel from one brand may not match another. Where you can, keep to one maker for the whole room.

Matching

Choosing tapware as a matched set

Pick one series and one finish, then choose each piece from it: the basin mixer, the shower mixer, the shower and the bath spout. Millennium series such as Cioso, Akemi and Jenex run across the mixers, spouts and showers.

For older style plumbing with separate hot and cold taps, see wall top assemblies and tap sets. Then add bath spouts and outlets and shower rails and twin showers in the same finish.

Ratings

WELS ratings and warranty

WELS is the national water efficiency label. More stars mean less water used, and the label also gives the flow in litres a minute. Where a maker publishes the rating, it is on the product page.

Each product carries its maker's warranty. ACL lists a warranty period on many of its products, and the period differs from one product to the next. Ask us for the terms of the tapware on your enquiry.

Where we are

Showroom and delivery

Showroom: 43-45 Bonnrigg Avenue, Bonnyrigg NSW 2177. We are open Monday to Friday 7am to 5pm and Saturday 7am to 3pm. We deliver across Sydney metro, and tapware can travel with your tiles and the rest of our bathroomware range.

Brands

ACL and Millennium tapware

Millennium supplies 921 of the tapware products in this section and ACL supplies 263. A further 30 come from Poseidon.

Millennium publishes a specification drawing and a technical data sheet for its products. Ask us for the sheet before your plumber roughs in, as it gives the set-out and the size of the hole in the wall or bench.

Care

Caring for tapware finishes

Wipe tapware with a soft damp cloth and mild soapy water, then dry it. That is all most finishes need.

Do not use cream cleansers, scourers, bleach or acid based cleaners. They strip coloured and brushed finishes and can void the maker's warranty.

Tapware

Tapware questions

Should all bathroom tapware match?

It looks best when it does. Keep one finish and, where you can, one series across the basin mixer, shower and bath spout. Accessories and the mirror frame can match the same finish.

What is the most durable tapware finish?

Chrome is the longest established finish and the easiest to match years later. Brushed finishes hide scratches and water marks well. Whatever the finish, gentle cleaning matters more than the colour.

What does a WELS rating mean?

WELS is Australia's water efficiency labelling scheme. The label shows a star rating and the flow in litres a minute. More stars mean the tap or shower uses less water.

How much does bathroom tapware cost?

The tapware in this section shows Enquire Now. Add the products to your enquiry and our team confirms the price for the model and finish you choose.

Is tapware covered by a warranty?

Yes. Each product carries its maker's warranty, and the period differs from one product to the next. Ask us for the terms of the tapware on your enquiry.

Can I see tapware finishes in the showroom?

Call (02) 8786 0288 before you visit and the team will tell you which finishes can be seen at the showroom. Showroom: 43-45 Bonnrigg Avenue, Bonnyrigg NSW 2177.

mainEntity.name: What is the most durable tapware finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chrome is the longest established finish and the easiest to match years later. Brushed finishes hide scratches and water marks well. Whatever the finish, gentle cleaning matters more than the colour.

mainEntity.name: What does a WELS rating mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: WELS is Australia's water efficiency labelling scheme. The label shows a star rating and the flow in litres a minute. More stars mean the tap or shower uses less water.
